newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ROBECO RAISES NLG 675 MLN WITH NEW EURO BOND FUNDS.
newsitem.headline: ROBECO RAISES NLG 675 MLN WITH NEW EURO BOND FUNDS.

text.p: The Robeco Group said on Tuesday it had raised a total of 675 million guilders with two new funds which are going to invest in euro denominated debt.

Robeco board member Hans Leenaars said the successful introduction of the RG Euro Bond Growth Fund and the RG Euro Bond Dividend Fund showed that private investors had confidence in the introduction of the common European currency.
"The euro will certainly come, the financial markets believe so and our customers are also clearly convinced of that," he said at a presentation of the two new mutual funds.

The funds will invest in bonds issued by countries which are seen joining the European Monetary Union from the start, namely the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Finland, France, Ireland, Luxembourg and Austria.
The average maturity of the loans is seven to eight years. The funds can also use derivatives such as options and futures. Until the start of the euro, all currency risks will be hedged.

The two new funds, alike except in their tax treatment for Dutch private investors, started trading today at their issue prices of 100 guilders for the RG Euro Bond Growth Fund and 50 guilders for the RG Euro Bond Dividend Fund.
Chairman George Moeller of the Amsterdam Stock Exchange welcomed the introduction of the two new funds, saying they offered more diversified investment opportunities.
"At a time when everybody seems to think that the bourse levels only can rise, it is appropriate that funds are also floated which would be suitable for a more defensive period," Moeller said.
